title: Carmen
by: Georges Bizet, 1875; libretto by Henri Meilhac and Ludovic Halévy
sung: sung in French, with English surtitles
note: The melody and the words are Bizet's (after Iradier's El arreglito), in the public domain; the voice and the orchestra are synthesised in the browser, and the English lines are this project's own. The notes are checked against Choudens's vocal score (Paris, plate A.C. 3082, the 1883 reprint of the 1875 edition, pp. 49-51): the verse is Carmen's; in the refrain the chorus of cigarières and young men sings the tune and she answers "L'amour!" over it before the couplet's end.
lines: L'amour est un oiseau rebelle
Love is a wild bird
Que nul ne peut apprivoiser,
that no one can tame,
Et c'est bien en vain qu'on l'appelle,
and you call it quite in vain
S'il lui convient de refuser.
if it chooses to refuse.
Rien n'y fait, menace ou prière,
Nothing works, threat or plea;
L'un parle bien, l'autre se tait;
one man talks well, the other is silent,
Et c'est l'autre que je préfère,
and it's the other one I prefer:
Il n'a rien dit, mais il me plaît.
he said nothing, but I like him.
L'amour est un oiseau rebelle
Love is a wild bird
Que nul ne peut apprivoiser,
that no one can tame,
Et c'est bien en vain qu'on l'appelle,
and you call it quite in vain
S'il lui convient de refuser.
if it chooses to refuse.
L'amour est enfant de Bohême,
Love is a gypsy child,
Il n'a jamais, jamais connu de loi;
it has never, ever known a law.
Si tu ne m'aimes pas, je t'aime;
If you don't love me, I love you;
Si je t'aime, prends garde à toi!
and if I love you, watch out!
Prends garde à toi!
Watch out!
source: Bizet, Carmen, vocal score, Paris: Choudens [1883], No. 5 Habanera, pp. 49-51 (Internet Archive carmenopracomi00bize, public domain)
